text: This is Lake McGregor, and on the 9th of August, 1968, a Mrs. L.M. Chase of Lowman, about five
miles east of Lake McGregor, for over two hours watched a very brilliant light move
up and down on Harvard and perform maneuvers over Lake McGregor.
She called her husband and her granddaughter, Kathy Richardson, and they all watched it.
They went outside at various times.
And when it was dropping, the lake, which was intensely blueish-white, would become brighter.
And it dropped very much faster than a plane would.
So it looks as if this visitor is coming back to the reservoir in southern Alberta.

would compare with, say, the four million that have been in that position.
Oh, it is much bigger than that.
Well, I have been asked about how big it was, or how far away it was.
Now, the only way I can judge, about one mile from us is a provincial park on the north side of the dam.
Halfway up from that park is a point from those, which we figure is halfway.
Then in between that half bay point and our home is a small bay called McCade Bay.
And it was just round about McCade Bay that this object veered and went up over the hill.
So that I would say, Judy, it was just about a quarter of a mile away.
And how high above the water is it?
As close as the point?
Well, it is pretty high to judge, but I would say between 50 to 100 feet.
Now you spoke of a white light. Did it have any tinge other than just pure white?
Yes, there was kind of a blue, a bluey sort of a tinge.
Something like the vapor lights that we have here in the seats, but there was just this kind of a bluey light.
Do you remember the weather conditions? Were there clouds or was it clear?
No, it was a very nice bright starlight night. That was why I was looking up. It wasn't bright.
It was a dark night, but there was a great many stars out.
And that is when I stood there before I went to bed and looked at the star of the east, and then again later.
Now when it lit up the wall, would you say it was as bright as a full moon illuminating the waters?
Yes, it would be. It would be as bright as that, except a harder light.
The full moon usually makes a golden light, but this made kind of a hot light.
